title: This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
gist: Linda Marsa describes the Prima retinal implant system from Science Corporation, approved in Europe in July and awaiting FDA clearance, which pairs a 378-pixel photovoltaic implant with camera glasses; more than 80% of recipients with advanced macular degeneration could read, do crosswords and use phones after training.

insights.claim: Age-related macular degeneration affects more than 5 million people worldwide, and until now no treatment could restore their vision.
insights.speaker: Linda Marsa
insights.so_what: Sizes the addressable patient population for retinal prostheses.

insights.claim: The Prima system was approved in Europe in July and is awaiting FDA clearance in the US; after training, more than 80% of recipients could read, do crosswords and use their phones.
insights.speaker: Linda Marsa
insights.so_what: FDA clearance is the next catalyst for Science Corporation; efficacy figure is as reported by the article.

insights.claim: Prima exploits the fact that AMD kills only photoreceptors while leaving other retinal circuitry intact, so the implant replaces photoreceptors and feeds signals to healthy bipolar and ganglion cells, leveraging the body's own processing.
insights.speaker: Linda Marsa
insights.so_what: Targeting a defined failure point lets a simple prosthesis restore function.
insights.quote: We’re leveraging all of the body’s own natural functions to process and transmit the information

insights.claim: Glasses with a front-facing camera capture roughly five megapixel video at 30 frames per second, a handheld processor converts it to infrared signals, and a laser projector pulses 880 nm near-infrared light through the pupil to the implant.
insights.speaker: Linda Marsa
insights.so_what: Describes the hardware stack; supply-chain exposure includes cameras, lasers and processors.

insights.claim: The implant has 378 pixels, each with an electrode and two photovoltaic cells that both convert light to current for the retina and act as solar cells powering the chip, eliminating the need for a battery.
insights.speaker: Linda Marsa
insights.so_what: A wireless, battery-free design reduces implant complexity and failure modes.
